grammar.title: Health and Wellbeing structures

lessons.title: At the pharmacy: a simple request
lessons.learn: Ask for a familiar medicine and explain one basic symptom without turning the exchange into a diagnosis.

grammar.title: దాతువు కావాలి and dative need
grammar.explain: Use నాకు for the person who needs something. Keep the object before కావాలి, then ask politely with కావాలా? A symptom can be stated separately; the phrase does not diagnose its cause.

examples.en: I need a tablet for fever.
Take this medicine twice a day.

mistakes.why: The question particle changes the meaning; use కావాలి for a statement of need.

dialogue.en: I need a tablet for fever.
Do you have an instruction from a doctor?
Yes, they said twice a day.
All right, please read the label too.

lessons.title: A short meeting invitation
lessons.learn: Invite a colleague to a brief meeting and make the time and place easy to confirm.

grammar.title: time phrases before the verb
grammar.explain: Telugu usually places time and place information before the final verb. Use రేపు with a clock time marked by గంటలకు; an invitation can end with వస్తారా? to ask respectfully.

examples.en: There is a meeting tomorrow at ten.
Is this room free for you?
Will you come to the meeting?

mistakes.why: మీరు takes respectful plural agreement వస్తారా, not familiar వస్తావా.

dialogue.t: రేపు పది గంటలకు చిన్న సమావేశం ఉంది.
dialogue.r: Rēpu padi gaṇṭalaku chinna samāvēśaṁ undi.
dialogue.en: There is a short meeting tomorrow at ten.
Which room should we meet in?
The room on the second floor is free.
All right, I will come on time.

culture.text: Telugu is written in its own left-to-right script. A consonant normally carries an inherent short a; a vowel sign changes that sound, and the virama (్) removes it or helps write a consonant cluster. A learner can therefore read a syllable by looking at the consonant and the mark attached to it, rather than treating every printed shape as an unrelated letter. Telugu and Kannada scripts also share a historical stage, though each is a distinct script and language.

reading.text: నా పేరు అనన్య. నేను విజయవాడలో ఉంటాను. మా ఇంట్లో తెలుగు పుస్తకాలు ఉన్నాయి. ఈ రోజు నేను అచ్చులు, హల్లులు చదువుతున్నాను. మా ఉపాధ్యాయుడు ఒక అక్షరాన్ని బోర్డుపై రాశారు. నేను దాన్ని పలికి, నా పుస్తకంలో మళ్లీ రాశాను. ఇప్పుడు చిన్న పదాలను నెమ్మదిగా చదవగలను.
reading.gloss: My name is Ananya. I live in Vijayawada. There are Telugu books in our home. Today I am reading vowels and consonants. Our teacher wrote one letter on the board. I pronounced it and wrote it again in my book. Now I can read short words slowly.

listening.script:
అనన్య: నమస్కారం, ఇది తెలుగు తరగతి ఎక్కడ?
ఉపాధ్యాయుడు: ఈ గది చివర ఉంది. నెమ్మదిగా రండి.
అనన్య: ధన్యవాదాలు. నేను కొత్త విద్యార్థిని.
ఉపాధ్యాయుడు: స్వాగతం. మీ పుస్తకం తెరవండి.

task.title: తెలుగు అక్షరాలతో స్వపరిచయం
task.instructions: Write six short Telugu sentences: your name, town, one person at home, a book you read, a letter you are practising, and a polite question to a classmate. Underline two vowel signs and one virama. Read the sentences slowly, then copy one of them without looking at the model.

pronunciation.t: Telugu distinguishes short and long vowels.
pronunciation.tip: Hold long vowels longer; vowel length can distinguish words.

pronunciation.t: ట డ ణ use a curled tongue.
pronunciation.tip: Curl the tongue tip back briefly for retroflex sounds.

pronunciation.t: త ద న are dental sounds.
pronunciation.tip: Touch the tongue lightly to the upper teeth.
Release a clear puff of air for the aspirated member.

pronunciation.t: Stress is gentle and syllables stay clear.
pronunciation.tip: Avoid heavy English stress; pronounce each written syllable evenly.

alphabet.title: Telugu Script Foundations
alphabet.explain: Round, looping letters — the curves come from writing on palm leaves, where straight cuts would tear the leaf. Left to right and fully phonetic: 16 vowels (short and long e/o matter!) and all the consonant rows Hindi has, plus extras like ళ and a second R (ఱ).

counting.title: Telugu Numbers
counting.explain: Telugu counts directly — but people get special number-words:
rules: Learn one to twenty as complete forms before combining larger numbers.
A numeral normally comes before the noun it counts.
